newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB launches wheat brands, claims world first.
newsitem.headline: AWB launches wheat brands, claims world first.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) is aiming to capture a greater slice of the international market by selling its wheat under brands in what the AWB called a "world first".
The move was officially launched by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade Tim Fischer at an industry function in Melbourne on Wednesday night.

"In a progressive marketing thrust more common to consumer companies like McDonalds and Kelloggs, Australian wheat is being marketed under brands, each targeted at discerning customers for specific end-uses," the AWB said in a statement.
"The branding strategy puts Australia at the cutting edge of grain marketing", the AWB said.
Brands will be built on quality gradings developed by the AWB through the national classification system.
Brands for Australian wheat are Soft, Prime Hard, Durum, Hard, Australian Standard White (ASW) and a wheat launched on Wednesday night, Premium White.
This was a very versatile wheat which had already gained wide market acceptance, the AWB said.
The brands capitalise on the unique white colour of Australian wheat and will be supported by an international promotional campaign under the slogan White Wheat Australian Gold, the AWB said.
"By branding our products and supporting them with a comprehensive quality programme, the AWB has built a competitive advantage in the international wheat market," AWB chairman Trevor Flugge said.
The new flagship brand ASW was a medium protein wheat designed for buyers who needed specific performance characteristics, he said.
It was also suitable for bulk buyers needing a single versatile product, he said.

Premium White was more versatile, had superior milling characteristics, excellent starch quality and better processing capability for products such as instant noodles, baked products and pan and flat breads, Flugge said.

The AWB had already identified international demand for about four million tonnes of Premium White a year, outgoing managing director John Lawrenson said. Premium White had become the benchmark for Australian White Wheat, he said.
